question: If a commercial vehicle is not equipped with electrical fuses, what must the driver do during the CDL vehicle inspection test?
choice_a: Mention this to the examiner and identify that the vehicle operates on circuit breakers
choice_b: Automatically fail that portion of the test
choice_c: Skip the emergency equipment section entirely
choice_d: Install temporary fuses before continuing
explanation: The manual states: "If the vehicle is not equipped with electrical fuses, you must mention this to the examiner and identify that the vehicle operates on circuit breakers."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection (Emergency Equipment)

question: What must a driver confirm about the fire extinguisher during the vehicle inspection?
choice_a: That it has a minimum 10-pound rating
choice_b: That it is properly charged and secured
choice_c: That it is mounted within reach of passengers
choice_d: That it was serviced within the last 90 days
explanation: The manual directs the driver to "Inspect for a properly charged and secured fire extinguisher."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection (Emergency Equipment)

question: Which combination of emergency warning devices satisfies the manual's requirement?
choice_a: Two red flags and one flare
choice_b: Four fusee flares and one triangle
choice_c: Three red reflective triangles, six fusee flares, or three liquid burning flares
choice_d: One liquid burning flare only
explanation: The manual specifies inspecting for "three (3) red reflective triangles, six (6) fusee flares, or three (3) liquid burning flares."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection (Emergency Equipment)

question: Besides being clean and undamaged, what is the only item the manual allows in the driver's windshield viewing area?
choice_a: A GPS mount
choice_b: A parking permit
choice_c: A tinted visor strip
choice_d: An inspection sticker
explanation: The manual states to "Inspect that the windshield is clean with no obstructions except for an inspection sticker."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection (Windshield and Traffic Monitoring Devices)

question: How must a driver demonstrate that the windshield wipers operate correctly during the inspection?
choice_a: By turning them on and off to show smooth operation
choice_b: By describing their operation without touching the controls
choice_c: By having the examiner operate them
choice_d: By checking the wiper fluid reservoir only
explanation: The manual requires the driver to "demonstrate wipers operate smoothly by turning them on and off."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection (Wipers/Washers)

question: Why does the manual say the defroster must be inspected?
choice_a: It prevents fuel line freezing
choice_b: It improves visibility, especially during cold weather
choice_c: It reduces engine wear over time
choice_d: It is only required on school buses
explanation: The manual states: "The defroster improves visibility, especially during cold weather."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection (Heater/Defroster)

question: According to the manual, what is the purpose of the horn that must function properly on the inspected vehicle?
choice_a: To signal backing maneuvers to nearby workers
choice_b: To test the vehicle's electrical charging system
choice_c: To warn other roadway users of your presence and avoid potential collisions
choice_d: To alert dispatch of vehicle location
explanation: The manual explains the horn "must function properly in order to warn other roadway users of your presence and avoid potential collisions."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection (Horn(s))

question: How is the parking brake check performed?
choice_a: By checking the dashboard warning light only
choice_b: By releasing the parking brake and coasting on a grade
choice_c: By flooring the accelerator with the parking brake set
choice_d: With the parking brake engaged, remove foot from the service brake and gently pull forward to see that it holds
explanation: The manual states: "With the parking brake engaged...remove foot from service brake and inspect that the parking brake will hold the vehicle by gently pulling forward with the parking brake on."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Parking and Trailer Brake Check

question: At what speed does the driver pull forward before applying the service brake during the service brake check?
choice_a: 20 mph
choice_b: 15 mph
choice_c: 10 mph
choice_d: 5 mph
explanation: The manual instructs: "Pull forward at 5 mph, apply the service (foot) brake and come to a complete stop."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Service Brake Check

question: What does it indicate if the vehicle pulls to either side or does not stop well during the service brake check?
choice_a: The tires need to be rotated
choice_b: The brakes may not be working correctly
choice_c: The wheel alignment needs service
choice_d: The load is improperly distributed
explanation: The manual states: "If the vehicle pulls to either side or does not stop well, the brakes may not be working correctly."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1 - Service Brake Check

question: What happens if a driver fails to explain and demonstrate all four parts of the air brake check correctly?
choice_a: A warning is given and the test continues
choice_b: Points are deducted but the test can still be passed
choice_c: It results in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test
choice_d: The examiner performs the remaining steps
explanation: The manual states: "Failure to explain and demonstrate (perform) all four (4) parts of the air brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Brake Check

topic: Air Gauge and Governor Cutout Check
question: According to the manual, at approximately what psi range does governor cutout occur?
explanation: The manual states cutout "will occur at approximately 120 - 140 psi OR level specified by the manufacturer."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Gauge and Governor Cutout Check

question: For a single vehicle (or trailer without air brakes), how much may the air pressure drop in one minute during the leakage rate test after stabilization?
choice_a: No more than three (3) pounds
choice_b: No more than one (1) pound
choice_c: No more than two (2) pounds
choice_d: No more than five (5) pounds
explanation: The manual states the air pressure should drop "no more than three (3) pounds in one (1) minute (single vehicle or trailer without airbrakes)."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Leakage Rate Test

question: For a combination vehicle, what is the maximum allowable air pressure drop in one minute during the air leakage rate test?
choice_a: Three (3) pounds
choice_b: Four (4) pounds
choice_c: Six (6) pounds
choice_d: Eight (8) pounds
explanation: The manual states the drop should not exceed "four (4) pounds in one (1) minute (combination vehicle) after initial stabilization."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Leakage Rate Test

question: At what air pressure should the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, and flag) activate?
choice_a: At exactly 100 psi
choice_b: Before air pressure drops below 30 psi
choice_c: Before air pressure drops below 55 psi
choice_d: Before air pressure drops below 90 psi
explanation: The manual states: "The low air warning devices (buzzer, light, and flag) should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Warning Device(s) Test

question: How does the driver fan off air pressure during the air warning device test?
choice_a: By opening the air tank drain cock
choice_b: By disconnecting the trailer air lines
choice_c: By restarting the engine several times
choice_d: By applying and releasing the foot brake without re-starting the engine
explanation: The manual states: "Without re-starting the engine...Begin fanning off the air pressure by applying and releasing the foot brake."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Air Warning Device(s) Test

question: Between what psi range should the parking (emergency) brake valve close (pop out), per the manual?
choice_a: 20 psi to 45 psi
choice_b: 10 psi to 20 psi
choice_c: 45 psi to 70 psi
choice_d: 70 psi to 90 psi
explanation: The manual states the valve "should close (pop out) between 20 psi and 45 psi (no less than 20 psi and no more than 45 psi) OR level specified by the manufacturer."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Emergency Brake(s) Test

question: On air-operated trailers, when should the tractor protection valve and trailer parking brake valve close relative to the truck/tractor/bus valve?
choice_a: Only well after the truck valve closes
choice_b: At the same time or prior to the valve for the truck/tractor/bus
choice_c: Exactly 10 psi after the truck valve closes
choice_d: There is no specified relationship
explanation: The manual states these valves "should close (pop out) at the same time or prior to the valve for the truck/tractor/bus."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Emergency Brake(s) Test

question: What is the consequence of failing to explain and demonstrate the hydraulic brake check correctly?
choice_a: A retest is scheduled later the same day
choice_b: A five-point deduction from the score
choice_c: It results in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test
choice_d: The examiner completes the check instead
explanation: The manual states: "Failure to explain and demonstrate the hydraulic brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: With the transmission in "park," how many times should the driver pump the brake pedal before holding it down during the hydraulic brake pressure check?
choice_a: Once
choice_b: Twice
choice_c: Five times
choice_d: Three times
explanation: The manual describes the check as "pump the brake pedal three (3) times, and then hold it down for five (5) seconds, or as specified by the manufacturer."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: What should NOT happen to the brake pedal after the initial application during the hydraulic brake check?
choice_a: It should move (depress) further
choice_b: It should feel firm
choice_c: It should have reserve pressure
choice_d: It should return to normal height when released
explanation: The manual states: "The brake pedal should not move (depress) after initial application and should be firm and have a sufficient amount of reserve for brake pedal application."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.1.2 - Hydraulic Brake Check

question: If a bus is equipped with a passenger lift, what must be true of the lift once the inspection is complete?
choice_a: It must be extended halfway for quick access
choice_b: It must be fully retracted and latched securely
choice_c: It must remain unlocked
choice_d: It must be removed from the vehicle
explanation: The manual states: "If equipped, lift must be fully retracted and latched securely."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.2 - Passenger Entry and Lift

question: How many emergency exits must the driver actually demonstrate operate smoothly, close securely, and are undamaged?
choice_a: None; description alone suffices
choice_b: Only the rear exit
choice_c: At least one (1)
choice_d: All emergency exits
explanation: The manual states: "Demonstrate that at least one (1) emergency exit operates smoothly, closes securely, and is not damaged... Point out and describe how all other emergency exits operate."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.2 - Emergency Exits

question: What must be inspected regarding passenger seat frames?
choice_a: That they recline smoothly
choice_b: That they are painted a uniform color
choice_c: That they have manufacturer labels attached
choice_d: That there are no broken seat frames and they are firmly attached to the floor
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that there are no broken seat frames and inspect that seat frames are firmly attached to the floor."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.2 - Passenger Seating

question: On a school bus, which additional type of mirror must be inspected beyond internal and external passenger mirrors?
choice_a: Student crossover mirrors
choice_b: Blind spot convex mirrors
choice_c: Rear bumper mirrors
choice_d: Dash-mounted vanity mirrors
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect student crossover mirrors (school bus only)."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.2 - Passenger Monitoring Devices

question: Which lights must be inspected on both the front and back of a school bus, per the Student Lights section?
choice_a: Only the headlights
choice_b: Strobe light (if equipped), alternately flashing amber lights, and alternately flashing red lights
choice_c: Only fog lights and hazard flashers
choice_d: Only the red lights
explanation: The manual requires inspecting the strobe light (if equipped), alternately flashing amber lights, and alternately flashing red lights on the front and back, along with their dash indicators.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.3 - Student Lights (Front and Back)

question: According to the manual, what is the purpose of the safety arm on a school bus?
choice_a: To keep the stop arm from retracting early
choice_b: To automatically dial emergency services
choice_c: To force school students to cross well (e.g., 10 feet) away from the front of the bus in the driver's view
choice_d: To activate the student lights automatically
explanation: The manual states: "Safety Arm - Forces school students to cross well (e.g., 10 feet) away from the front of the school bus in the drivers view."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.3 - Stop Arm(s) and Safety Arm

topic: First Aid Emergency and Body Fluid Kits
question: What should a driver check regarding the seal on the emergency first aid kit?
choice_a: That the seal is a specific color
choice_b: That the seal has an expiration date printed on it
choice_c: That the seal was applied by a certified inspector
choice_d: That the seal has not been broken, which may indicate missing items
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that emergency first aid kit is present and the seal has not been broken which may indicate missing items."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.3 - First Aid Emergency and Body Fluid Kits

question: From where must the operation of all external lights be inspected?
choice_a: From outside the vehicle
choice_b: From inside the vehicle only
choice_c: From the examiner's own vehicle
choice_d: Using dashboard indicators alone
explanation: The manual states: "The operation of all external lights must be inspected from outside the vehicle, including lights activated by an automated light check system."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.4 - Lights Operations Check

question: What must brake lights do according to the Lights Operations Check?
choice_a: Stay on continuously regardless of brake application
choice_b: Come "on" when the brakes are applied and turn "off" when the brakes are released
choice_c: Flash intermittently whenever the vehicle is moving
choice_d: Only illuminate when the parking brake is set
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that brake lights come 'on' when brakes are applied and turn 'off' when brakes are released."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.4 - Lights Operations Check

question: What must be true of light lenses or covers on the front of the vehicle?
choice_a: They must have manufacturer stamps clearly visible
choice_b: They must be tinted to reduce glare
choice_c: They must be the proper color, clean, not broken and not missing
choice_d: They must be made of glass rather than plastic
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that light lenses or covers are the proper color, clean, not broken and not missing."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Lenses

question: Which fluid levels must the driver indicate would be inspected, with the engine off?
choice_a: Transmission fluid and windshield washer fluid only
choice_b: Only engine oil and diesel exhaust fluid
choice_c: Only brake fluid
choice_d: Engine oil, cooling system/coolant, power steering fluid, and brake fluid (hydraulic brakes only)
explanation: The manual lists engine oil, cooling system/coolant, power steering fluid, and brake fluid (hydraulic brakes only) as the fluids to inspect with the engine off.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Critical Fluid Levels

question: Besides looking for puddles on the ground, what else should the driver check for regarding fluid leaks?
choice_a: Dripping fluids around and on the underside of the engine and transmission
choice_b: Excess tread wear on the tires
choice_c: Odometer discrepancies
choice_d: Exhaust smoke color
explanation: The manual states: "Look for dripping fluids around and on underside of engine and transmission."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Fluid and Air Leaks

question: What must be inspected about the power steering box?
choice_a: That it matches the frame color
choice_b: That it is securely mounted and not leaking
choice_c: That it carries a visible warranty sticker
choice_d: That it can be removed without tools
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that the power steering box is securely mounted and not leaking."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.1 - Steering System

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on steering axle tires, per the manual?
choice_a: 2/32 inch
choice_b: 3/32 inch
choice_c: 4/32 inch
choice_d: 6/32 inch
explanation: The manual specifies minimum tread depth on "major tread grooves containing wear bars (4/32 on steering axle tires, 2/32 on all other tires)."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Tires

question: What is the minimum tread depth required on tires other than the steering axle tires?
choice_a: 3/32 inch
choice_b: 4/32 inch
choice_c: 5/32 inch
choice_d: 2/32 inch
explanation: The manual states the minimum tread depth is "2/32 on all other tires," compared to 4/32 on steering axle tires.
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Tires

question: What does the manual say about checking tire inflation by kicking the tires or using a mallet?
choice_a: It must always precede using a tire gauge
choice_b: It is acceptable only on dual tires
choice_c: It is a recognized quick alternative to a tire gauge
choice_d: The driver will not get credit; the use of a tire gauge must be mentioned
explanation: The manual states: "You will not get credit if you simply kick the tires or use a mallet to inspect for proper inflation. You must mention the use of a tire gauge."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Tires

question: What does the manual say about welding repairs on rims?
choice_a: Rims cannot have welding repairs
choice_b: Welding repairs are acceptable if certified
choice_c: Welding repairs are only prohibited on trailer rims
choice_d: Welding repairs must be documented in the vehicle file
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect for damaged, cracked, or bent rims. Rims cannot have welding repairs."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Rims

question: What signs might indicate that lug nuts are loose, per the manual?
choice_a: A visible torque wrench mark
choice_b: Discoloration of the rim only
choice_c: Rust trails or shiny threads
choice_d: Excess grease buildup on the nut
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that lug nuts are not loose and there are no signs of rust trails or shiny threads that may show looseness."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Lug Nuts

question: What must the driver check for regarding brake contaminates, if accessible?
choice_a: Rust on the brake drum exterior only
choice_b: Paint overspray on the brake shoes
choice_c: Water pooling in the brake fluid reservoir
choice_d: Contaminants such as grease or oil on the brake lining or pads and the brake drum or disc
explanation: The manual states: "If accessible, inspect for contaminants such as grease, oil, etc., on the brake lining or pads and the brake drum or disc that can affect braking capabilities."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Brake Contaminates

question: What should the driver do if the batteries are not visible or accessible during the inspection?
choice_a: Skip the item without comment
choice_b: Assume the batteries are functioning properly
choice_c: Inform the examiner and describe what is being inspected
choice_d: Request a different test vehicle
explanation: The manual states: "Inform the examiner if the batteries are not visible or accessible. If they are not visible or accessible, you should describe what you are inspecting."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Battery

question: What must be inspected regarding the fuel tank, including the DEF tank if equipped?
choice_a: That the tank material is aluminum
choice_b: That it is filled to at least half capacity
choice_c: That it is painted a reflective color
choice_d: That it is securely mounted, the cap is tight, and there are no leaks from the tank or line
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that the fuel tank, including a Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) tank, if equipped, is securely mounted, the cap is tight, and there are no leaks from the tank or line."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Fuel Tank/DEF Tank

question: What must be inspected regarding the trailer tandem release lever and pins, if applicable?
choice_a: That they are removed prior to inspection
choice_b: That they are painted a bright color
choice_c: That they are secure
choice_d: That they are lubricated weekly
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that trailer tandem release lever and pins are secure, if applicable."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.5.2 - Frame(s)

question: What must be inspected about the fifth wheel skid plate's mounting?
choice_a: That it has a manufacturer certification tag
choice_b: That it is removable for cleaning
choice_c: That it is bolted with a minimum number of bolts specified by law
choice_d: That it is securely mounted to the vehicle by the fifth wheel platform
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that the fifth wheel skid plate is securely mounted to the vehicle by the fifth wheel platform."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Fifth Wheel Skid Plate

question: What should the driver inspect regarding the space between the apron and the fifth wheel?
choice_a: That a small gap exists for lubrication flow
choice_b: That the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no gap between the apron and fifth wheel
choice_c: That the gap measures exactly one inch
choice_d: Gap inspection is only required on pintle hook combinations
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate and there is no space between the apron and fifth wheel (no gap)."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Kingpin, Apron & Gap

question: What must be inspected about the pintle hook's mounting, for pintle hook combinations?
choice_a: That it is securely mounted to the vehicle frame
choice_b: That it swivels freely in every direction
choice_c: That it is painted a specific safety color
choice_d: That it is greased before every trip
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that the pintle hook is securely mounted to the vehicle frame."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Pintle Hook

question: What must the trailer tongue be able to do, according to the manual's drawbar ring and tongue inspection?
choice_a: Rotate 360 degrees for coupling
choice_b: Detach automatically in a rollover
choice_c: Support the weight of the load
choice_d: Fold flat for storage
explanation: The manual states to inspect the trailer tongue "for dents, twists, cracks, and broken welds and that the trailer tongue can support the weight of the load."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Trailer Drawbar Ring & Tongue

question: What three conditions must be verified about the trailer coupler under 'All Other Types of Combinations'?
choice_a: That it is chrome-plated, lubricated, and painted
choice_b: That it is removable, adjustable, and lightweight
choice_c: That it is insured, registered, and labeled
choice_d: That it is not bent or twisted, is secured to the trailer tongue with no loose or missing bolts, and is not worn
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that the trailer coupler is not bent or twisted... is secured to the trailer tongue and there are no loose or missing bolts, broken welds, or cracks... is not worn."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Trailer Coupler & Tongue

topic: Locking and Safety Devices - Fifth Wheel
question: For fifth wheel coupling systems, what should the driver check when looking into the fifth wheel gap?
choice_a: That the locking jaws or lever are fully secured around the kingpin with no play
choice_b: That the gap is filled with grease only
choice_c: That the kingpin has been removed for cleaning
choice_d: That the locking jaws are painted red
explanation: The manual states: "Look into fifth wheel gap and inspect that locking jaws or lever are fully secured around the kingpin and inspect for play between kingpin and locking jaws/lever."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Locking and Safety Devices (Fifth Wheel Coupling Systems)

topic: Locking and Safety Devices - All Other Systems
question: For coupling systems other than fifth wheel, what must be true of breakaway cables?
choice_a: They may be disconnected during a routine inspection
choice_b: They must be engaged
choice_c: They are optional on trailers under 10,000 pounds
choice_d: They must be replaced every 12 months
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that safety cables or chains are secure, crossed, and free of kinks and excessive slack, if present. Breakaway cables must be engaged."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.6.1 - Locking and Safety Devices (All Other Coupling Systems)

question: What position must the landing gear be in for travel, per the manual?
choice_a: Partially lowered for stability
choice_b: Fully lowered
choice_c: Fully raised
choice_d: Removed from the trailer
explanation: The manual states: "Inspect that the landing gear is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.6.2 - Landing Gear & Clearance

question: According to the manual, for which vehicle type is reflective tape required?
choice_a: Straight trucks only
choice_b: Passenger cars
choice_c: Buses only
choice_d: Trailers
explanation: The manual notes: "Reflective tape is only required for trailers. Some jurisdictional laws may require reflective tape for school buses."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11.6.2 - Reflective Tape

question: On the Class A, B, and C checklists, which item is marked with an asterisk indicating automatic failure if not performed correctly?
choice_a: The air or hydraulic brake check
choice_b: The reflective tape check
choice_c: The frame inspection
choice_d: The lights operations check
explanation: The checklists mark "*air or *hydraulic brake check" with the note "* Automatic failure if not performed correctly."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11 - Class A/B/C Vehicle Inspection Checklists

question: What must a driver do for each safety critical item to receive credit during the inspection test?
choice_a: Only point to the item silently
choice_b: Name, point to and/or touch, and fully explain what is being inspected
choice_c: Photograph the item for the record
choice_d: Ask the examiner to confirm the item verbally
explanation: The manual states: "You MUST name, point to and/or touch, and fully explain what you are inspecting each safety critical item for. If you do not do so, you will not get credit for the item(s)."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection Checklist rules

question: What must happen before a driver can proceed to the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: The written knowledge test must be retaken
choice_b: A road observer must approve the test route
choice_c: The Vehicle Inspection test must be passed
choice_d: The vehicle must be refueled to full
explanation: The manual states: "Remember, the Vehicle Inspection test must be passed before you can proceed to the Basic Control Skills test."
source_note: Rhode Island CDL Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection (Basic Control Skills Test)
